messages:
IncidentBot: paging alert: streaming decode pipeline p99 spike detected in us-west-2 fleet. Metric: decode_stream_latency.p99 = 1.42s (SLO 0.5s). Affected route: /v1/generate/stream (rwd-13b-quant).
Alex (oncall): ack — I'm on it. tagging @Jamie and @Liz.
Jamie (sre): seeing correlated disk page-fault churn and sudden enqueue latency on the decode worker VMs. p95 jumped from 320ms -> 780ms over last 10m. p99 at 1.4s.
Liz (eng_runtime): confirming, playback trace shows streaming stalls at the first token decode page fault path. KV cache lookups are OK, but decode kernel is backing up.
Sam (eng_kernel): fyi a kernel push rolled to a subset of nodes at 02:14 UTC: kernel-5.14-rt2+patch. There was a change to page allocator heuristics and CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT tweaks. Could interact with our userspace TRT/FlashAttention memory touch patterns.
Alex (oncall): copy. How many nodes affected?
Jamie (sre): ~34/420 nodes in us-west-2, all on the new kernel build. Traffic fraction ~3% but those hosts are in hot pools so impact visible to p99.
Maya (customer_success): we've received 3 support tickets from streaming customers, one reported intermittent disconnects and one timeout at 30s. CS flagged severity-high.
Liz (eng_runtime): stack traces show the slow path hits in decode: flashattn fallback to slower kernel path. When FlashAttention path fails it falls back to a safe kernel codepath that is much slower. We're seeing increased syscalls around anonymous page faults.
Sam (eng_kernel): reproducer: running a memory-touch stress with flashattn-like access pattern shows increased page faults on kernel-5.14-rt2 on machines with older glibc. I suspect a subtle allocator alignment regression.
InfraOpsBot: host list for affected nodes: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b1, i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b1c2... (truncated).
Jamie (sre): mitigation options: 1) cordon and drain affected nodes and route traffic away; 2) roll back kernel to previous stable build for the small pool; 3) disable FlashAttention optimized path temporarily at runtime to force baseline kernel path across all nodes (safer but higher median latency).
Alex (oncall): what's fastest to reduce p99 now?
Liz (eng_runtime): fastest: route traffic off affected hosts (cordon + scale up unaffected pool) then roll back kernel. Disabling FlashAttention at runtime needs a full rollout and causes median regressions — risky for overall latency.
Sam (eng_kernel): I can prepare a rollback to kernel-5.14-rt1 and a hotpatch to revert the allocator tweak. Rollback ETA ~12m once infra approves.
Jamie (sre): I'll start draining the 34 nodes and request scale-up of 40 healthy nodes in the same region. Initiating now.
Alex (oncall): Jamie: please post commands and status updates here. Sam: put the rollback package in the kernel rollback bucket and ping @InfraOpsBot.
Sam (eng_kernel): rollback package uploaded: s3://kernels/rollback/5.14-rt1/176888. Command to trigger rollback via infra:
```
infra-ctl nodes set-kernel --nodes @affected --kernel s3://kernels/rollback/5.14-rt1/bootimg
infra-ctl reboot --nodes @affected --grace 30
```
Sam (eng_kernel): note: plan B is a targeted reboot into previous image; plan A is to hotpatch allocator (longer test).
InfraOpsBot: rollback job scheduled. batch size 6 nodes / 6m to avoid mass disruption.
Jamie (sre): drain progress: 6/34 drained, rerouting 0.8% of traffic so far. p99 improved to 0.9s on global aggregates but us-west-2 still at 1.1s.
Maya (customer_success): will notify the 3 affected customers that we're actively mitigating and expect partial recovery in ~30m.
Liz (eng_runtime): quick telemetry note: turning off FlashAttention fallback detection in the loader could avoid entering the slow fallback, but that requires a code change and rollout — not immediate.
Alex (oncall): agreed. proceed with kernel rollback. After rollback completes, we'll monitor p95/p99 for 30m before marking incident resolved. Sam, stay on-call for validation.
Sam (eng_kernel): rollback batches 1-4 completed (24 nodes). final batch 5 in progress.
Jamie (sre): last batch done. all 34 nodes now back on kernel-5.14-rt1. Rebalancing traffic.
InfraOpsBot: hosts rebooted and healthy checks passing.
Jamie (sre): metrics: us-west-2 decode p95 now 340ms, p99 540ms — back within SLOs. Streaming tail stalls reduced to baseline.
Maya (customer_success): customers updated; one confirmed the timeout no longer reproduces.
Alex (oncall): good work. Postmortem: cause hypothesis = kernel page-allocator tweak in kernel-5.14-rt2 interacting with FlashAttention memory access patterns causing increased page fault latencies and fallback path thrashing. Action items:
- Sam: prepare a repro report and patch candidate (due today EOD).
- Liz: add a runtime flag to quickly disable FlashAttention fallback per-pool (due 48h).
- Jamie: add a pipeline alarm to correlate kernel-version rollouts with p99 spikes (due 24h).
- Maya: follow-up customer notes + SLA credit assessment (due 24h).
Alex (oncall): tagging next oncall @Sam for kernel follow-up and @Liz for runtime fixes. Handoff to next oncall at 08:00 PST.
Sam (eng_kernel): I'll stay on until rollback verified and push repro + patch draft.
Liz (eng_runtime): will start the runtime feature and schedule a canary.
Alex (oncall): closing thread for now, will reopen if p99 creeps. :white_check_mark:
